children.value: One metric at a time. District below z12.5, neighborhood/dong above — same metric, detail swaps by zoom.
Each button toggles its layer on or off. Tap any pin or line on the map for its detail.
Walk minutes to the nearest station, on OSM footpaths. Auto = coarse cells out wide, fine cells past z14.
Every layer here is a model estimate, not a measurement.

Travel-ease = 0.4 area-centrality + 0.3 destination-access + 0.3 walk-ease. Destination access = average minutes to reach a district from all 24 others (kr_district_od), blended 50/50 with centrality; districts only, and the Best spots input.
Walk access: OSM footpaths at 4.8 km/h, no crossing delays; OSM vintage 2026-07-28; gray = no walkable path; central-Seoul bbox only (DATA_SOURCES.md).
Station walk-stress is a coordinate-only proxy. National KTX/SRT rail lives on the Korea screen. The Reach tab has the boundary-free heat view.
Estimate · tap a dot for scores
Web-verified events · sources in each entry

Reach tab: pick an origin hub, a time budget and a mode; the map colors how far you can get. Colored fills are district/neighborhood scores — darker/warmer usually means higher on that score (each layer's own legend is on the Map tab's Show/Hide buttons). Colored dots are stations or events. Best spots, Stations and Timeline cards carry the SAME tier colors as a left-edge stripe or leading dot (gray → teal → amber → blue → green, low to high; Timeline uses amber/teal/coral for Aug/Sep/Oct) — so a glance tells you the tier without opening a card. Tap a layer's Show/Hide button on the Map tab to toggle it; tap a card to see its full scores. The Reach explorer's origin is one of 8 precomputed hub stations (tap a tab above the map to switch) — the underlying matrix is only computed from these 8, so there's no free-tap-anywhere origin in this build. The faint grey fill under every reach map is the full city extent: it never disappears, so when you pull the time-budget slider down, cells beyond your budget read as neutral grey instead of vanishing — only the colored (in-budget) cells are affected by the slider.

Estimated travel access across Seoul (471-station subway graph, 25 districts, 424 neighborhoods) plus a national KTX/SRT rail overview, an Aug-Oct 2026 events timeline, and a network-ROUTED walk-access-to-nearest-station heatmap (fine + coarse grid cells; the WALKING route to that station follows real OSM footpaths/streets, not straight-line rings — but which station counts as “nearest” for a given cell is a separate, straight-line/haversine pick, not the fastest-arriving one; see the honesty caveats below). All scores are model ESTIMATES built by tool/korea/build_krtravel.py + build_krtravel_assets.py + build_krtravel_content.py + build_hexwalk.py from the same OSM-derived graph the Urbanset (terrain) applet uses. Map, Stations and Timeline screens each offer a Map ⇄ List (⇄ Calendar on Timeline) view — same underlying data, different lens.

transit_stress_score = unweighted betweenness centrality on the 471-node/587-edge subway graph, min-max normalized, quintile tier. walk_stress_score is a HONEST PROXY (nearby-station density only — NOT sidewalks/terrain/pedestrian network), flagged walk_stress_is_proxy on every station. area_centrality_score = 0.5×mean member station transit-stress + 0.5×normalized closeness; zero-station areas get tier "no-data" and score null, never interpolated. inbound_access_score (destination-access) = normalized negative mean ETA arriving at a district from all 24 others (kr_district_od, 25x25 avg-minutes matrix) — district-level only, no dong-level OD matrix this round. best_spots_score = 0.5×destination-access + 0.5×area-centrality. travel_ease_score (district) = 0.4×area-centrality + 0.3×destination-access + 0.3×walk-ease; (dong, no OD table at this granularity) = 0.6×area-centrality + 0.4×walk-ease. National rail lines are SCHEMATIC straight-line edges between named-route stations, not real track alignment, with minutes derived from an assumed 160 km/h effective speed (matches real Seoul-Busan KTX/SRT scheduled run times, not the 305 km/h design top speed). Reach explorer minutes come from two precomputed 471x471 station matrices (subway-only, and subway + the schematic national-rail layer), Dijkstra at 33 km/h + 0.5 min dwell per hop, quantized to whole minutes and CAPPED at 120 — a "120+" station is at the cap or has no route at all, never a literal count beyond it. Rail-combo join assumption: a national station becomes a transfer hub only where it falls within 1.5 km of a subway station — only 7 of the 45 do (Seoul Station, Yongsan, Cheongnyangni, Suseo, Gwangmyeong, Sangbong, Yangpyeong); the other 38 (Busan, Daegu, Gwangju, all 20km+ away) are NOT joined and never interpolated. Crossing networks at a joined hub costs a flat 8-minute transfer penalty each way (stated assumption — walk + wait/interchange, schematic, not timetable-exact). Bus is not modeled at all and is never approximated from subway/rail. NEAREST-STATION ASSIGNMENT CAVEAT (plain words): every walk cell and reach cell boards the subway at the straight-line-nearest station to its center, which may not be the station a real walk would actually arrive at fastest — so a cell's shown walk/reach time can understate the real one when the true fastest station isn't the closest one. BUCKET-TIER CAVEAT (plain words): the Reach Explorer's map colors and time-budget slider use 8 coarse tiers (<10/10-20/20-30/30-45/45-60/60-90/90-120/120+), an ABSOLUTE reading from the origin (never relative to the slider position) with a NEUTRAL grey for the 120+/no-route tier so an unreachable cell never reads as fast -- not exact continuous minutes, to keep the cell data compact (full formula above). HEAT-VIEW CAVEAT (plain words): the Heat toggle renders the SAME 8-tier bucketed values as a spatially kernel-blended gradient (seoul-true-heat round) -- smoother to look at, matching the Walk Score aesthetic, but not higher-resolution data: it blends the same coarse tiers across neighboring cells, it does not reveal exact continuous minutes any more than Buckets does.

Seoul subway stations, subway network, districts and neighborhoods: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL — reused from apps/terrain (same obligation applies here). Walk-access pedestrian network: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL, fetched fresh 2026-07-28 for this round (tool/korea/build_hexwalk.py). National rail station identity/coordinates: Wikipedia, web-verified 2026-07-28 (not independently copyrightable). Events: web-verified 2026-07-28 against official/tourism-board/press/Wikipedia sources per event — see each card's source note. Full formulas + every honesty caveat: DATA_SOURCES.md, section "terrain krtravel".

Round 1 built 2026-07-28 (krtravel-0728): no re-fetch, reuses apps/terrain content.json (kr_stations, kr_district_od) and geometry (network.geojson, seoul_districts.geojson, seoul_dong.geojson). Round 2 (hexwalk-0728, seedVersion 2026-07-28.3): fresh OSM pedestrian-network fetch (tool/korea/build_hexwalk.py) for the walk-access-to-nearest-station heatmap. Round 3 (designpass-0728, seedVersion 2026-07-28.4): UX rebuild — zoom-paired area layers (travel-ease + area-centrality), a dedicated Stations screen (map/list), a calendar/map/list Timeline, best-spots rank+score display, trimmed captions. No new data fetched.
